preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (deployer)
At least one user must hold some NMETA tokens

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setMaxTxAmount(0) to set the maximum transaction amount to zero. This will cause all subsequent transfer() and transferFrom() calls to fail due to the require(amount <= maxTxAmount) check in _transfer(), effectively locking all user funds in the contract.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The NowMeta contract has an owner-only function setMaxTxAmount() that controls the maximum transaction amount. When set to 0, the require(amount <= maxTxAmount) check in _transfer() will fail for any amount > 0, effectively locking all user funds. This is a classic owner privilege abuse where the owner can freeze all transfers.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner and call setMaxTxAmount(0) to set the maximum transaction amount to zero, which will block all transfers.
attempts.step_by_step_plan:
1. Identify the current owner address
2. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the owner
3. Call setMaxTxAmount(0) on the target contract
4. Verify that maxTxAmount is now 0
